'''Jonas Jerebko''' ({{IPA|sv|ˈjuːnas jɛˈrɛbːkʊ}}; born March 2, 1987) is a Swedish former professional [[basketball]] player. He was selected as the 39th overall pick in the second round of the [[2009 NBA draft]] by the [[Detroit Pistons]], becoming the second Swedish-born basketball player (after [[Miles Simon]]) to be selected in the [[NBA draft]]. Jerebko played a total of 10 seasons in the NBA with four different teams, the [[Detroit Pistons]], [[Boston Celtics]], [[Utah Jazz]] and [[Golden State Warriors]].

==Early life==
As a child growing up in Sweden, Jerebko was involved in many sports, but he excelled at basketball. Having parents who played basketball was good for Jerebko because there was very little interest in the game among his friends. He moved to [[Massachusetts]] during his senior year for a better opportunity. He attended [[Norwood High School (Massachusetts)|Norwood High School]] for his senior year and would impress on the court, receiving a few different offers.<ref name=mlive>{{cite web |url=http://www.mlive.com/pistons/index.ssf/2009/10/jerebko_gets_early_assist_from.html |title=New Piston Jonas Jerebko hopes NBA catches on in Sweden |first=A. Sherrod |last=Blakely |work=MLive.com |date=October 1, 2009 |access-date=February 14, 2016}}</ref>

In 2005, Jerebko signed to play basketball at the [[Buffalo Bulls men's basketball|University at Buffalo]] in his father's hometown. Ultimately, he gave up a basketball scholarship for a professional career.<ref name="Fraschilla">{{cite web |last=Fraschilla |first=Fran |authorlink=Fran Fraschilla |date=May 20, 2009 |title=NBA draft: Top 5 European prospects |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2009/columns/story?columnist=fraschilla_fran&page=nbadraft-090520 |access-date=June 3, 2023 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Europe (2005–2009)===
Jerebko began his career playing with second-tiered Swedish club [[Borås Basket]] in the 2005–06 season before joining first-tiered Swedish club [[LF Basket Norrbotten|Plannja Basket]] for the 2006–07 season. He averaged 20.0 points, 11.6 rebounds and 2.6 blocks in 19 games for Borås, and 10.0 points and 5.0 rebounds in 22 games for Plannja.

In 2007, Jerebko moved to Italy where he joined [[Angelico Biella]], playing for the club for two seasons.

===Detroit Pistons (2009–2015)===
[[File:JonasJerebko.jpg|thumb|Jerebko with the Pistons in 2009]]
In May 2009, [[ESPN]] analyst [[Fran Fraschilla]] considered Jerebko one of the top five European prospects in the [[2009 NBA draft]].<ref name="Fraschilla"/> He was subsequently selected with the 39th overall pick by the [[Detroit Pistons]], becoming the second Swedish national player to be selected in the NBA after the Swedish-born American [[Miles Simon]]. His career in the NBA got off to a rough-and-tumble start; in a preseason game, Jerebko was accused of punching [[Miami Heat]] center [[Jamaal Magloire]] in the face. Both players were suspended for the opening game of the regular season game for the ensuing fight.<ref>{{cite web |last=Watson |first=Matt |date=October 8, 2009 |title=Detroit's fighting Swede penalized |url=https://www.detroitbadboys.com/2009/10/8/1216838/detroits-fighting-swede-penalized |access-date=February 14, 2016 |work=detroitbadboys.com}}</ref> Jerebko's hustle and determination early on in 2009–10 made him a fan favorite. He was selected as a member of the Rookie Team as part of the 2010 Rookie Challenge and Youth Jam during the NBA All-Star Weekend. He appeared in 80 games (73 starts) for the Pistons as a rookie, averaging 9.3 points (.481 FG, .313 3FG), 6.0 rebounds, 0.7 assists and 0.99 steals in 27.9 minutes per game. He was among NBA rookie leaders ranked third in rebounds, fourth in blocks (0.36 bpg), fifth in minutes (27.9 mpg), eighth in steals, 10th in scoring and tied for 18th in assists. His 73 games as a starter ranks second in franchise history amongst rookies behind [[Kelly Tripucka]] who started all 82 games during the [[1981–82 Detroit Pistons season|1981–82 season]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/playerfile/jonas_jerebko/bio/ |title=Jonas Jerebko Stats, Video, Bio, Profile |work=NBA.com |access-date=February 14, 2016}}</ref>

On October 5, 2010, Jerebko strained his right Achilles' tendon in a preseason game against the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Langlois |first=Keith |url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/features/DETMIA_recap_101005.html |title=Heat Check; Jerebko's injury casts dark cloud over Pistons' preseason-opening loss |work=NBA.com |date=October 5, 2010 |access-date=February 14, 2016}}</ref> He subsequently missed the entire [[2010–11 Detroit Pistons season|2010–11 season]].

On December 9, 2011, Jerebko re-signed with the Pistons on a four-year, $16 million deal.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/jerebko_resign_111212.html |title=Pistons Re-Sign Forward Jonas Jerebko|work=NBA.com |date=December 9, 2011 |access-date=December 9, 2011}}</ref>

===Boston Celtics (2015–2017)===
On February 19, 2015, Jerebko was traded, along with [[Luigi Datome]], to the [[Boston Celtics]] in exchange for [[Tayshaun Prince]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-acquire-thomas-phoenix|title=Celtics Acquire Thomas From Phoenix|work=NBA.com|date=February 19, 2015|access-date=February 19, 2015}}</ref>

On July 9, 2015, Jerebko re-signed with the Celtics.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/boston-celtics-resign-jonas-jerebko|title=Boston Celtics Resign Jonas Jerebko|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2015|access-date=July 10, 2015}}</ref>

===Utah Jazz (2017–2018)===
On July 17, 2017, Jerebko signed with the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-forward-jonas-jerebko|title=Jazz Sign Forward Jonas Jerebko|work=NBA.com|date=July 17, 2017|access-date=July 17, 2017}}</ref> On July 7, 2018, he was waived by the Jazz.<ref>{{cite web|author=Utah Jazz|url=https://twitter.com/utahjazz/status/1015626534315364354|title=We've waived Jonas Jerebko.|work=Twitter|date=July 7, 2018|access-date=July 7, 2018}}</ref>

===Golden State Warriors (2018–2019)===
On July 12, 2018, Jerebko signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-free-agent-forward-jonas-jerebko|title=Warriors Sign Free Agent Forward Jonas Jerebko|work=NBA.com|date=July 12, 2018|access-date=July 12, 2018}}</ref> On October 19, he [[Basketball moves#Putback and tip-in|tipped in]] a shot against his former team with 0.3 seconds remaining to lift the Warriors to a 124–123 victory over the Jazz.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070220|title=Jerebko, Durant lead Warriors past Jazz 124-123|work=ESPN.com|date=October 19, 2018|access-date=October 21, 2018}}</ref> On November 13, he posted his 11th career [[double-double]] with season bests of 14 points and 14 rebounds in a 110–103 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070882|title=Kevin Durant leads undermanned Warriors past Hawks 110-103|work=ESPN.com|date=November 13, 2018|access-date=November 14, 2018}}</ref> On December 22, he scored a career-high 23 points on 10-for-12 shooting with six rebounds in 21 minutes off the bench in a 120–116 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071165|title=Durant scores 29 points, Warriors hold of Mavericks 120-116|work=ESPN.com|date=December 22, 2018|access-date=December 23, 2018}}</ref> The Warriors made it to the [[2019 NBA Finals]], where they were defeated by the [[Toronto Raptors]] in six games.

===Khimki (2019–2021)===
On August 14, 2019, Jerebko signed with [[BC Khimki|Khimki]] of the [[VTB United League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/khimki-moscow-signs-jonas-jerebko/|title=Khimki Moscow signs Jonas Jerebko|date=August 14, 2019|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 14, 2019|archive-date=August 14, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190814133430/https://sportando.basketball/en/khimki-moscow-signs-jonas-jerebko/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 23, 2021, Khimki terminated his contract, reportedly for personal reasons.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-01-23|title=Khimki parts ways with Greg Monroe and Jonas Jerebko|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1160170/khimki-parts-ways-with-greg-monroe-and-jonas-jerebko/|access-date=2021-01-29|website=Eurohoops|language=en}}</ref>

===CSKA Moscow (2022)===
On March 30, 2022, Jerebko signed with [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] for the rest of the season. The news of the signing, which occurred one month after the start of the [[Russian invasion of Ukraine]], was met with widespread criticism in his home country Sweden. He was swiftly suspended from the Sweden national team, and at least one of his main sponsors terminated his contract.<ref name="m.basketnews.com">{{Cite web|url=https://m.basketnews.com/news-169231-jonas-jerebko-gets-expelled-from-swedish-nt-after-signing-with-cska.html|title = Jonas Jerebko gets expelled from Swedish NT after signing with CSKA}}</ref> On June 18, 2022, Jerebko left CSKA Moscow.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ex-NBA Star Jonas Jerebko Leaves CSKA Moscow |url=https://www.news18.com/news/sports/ex-nba-star-jonas-jerebko-leaves-cska-moscow-5398471.html |access-date=January 22, 2023 |website=News 18}}</ref>

===Santeros de Aguada (2024)===
On March 13, 2024, Jerebko signed with the [[Santeros de Aguada]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Former Golden State Warriors Player Signs With New Team|url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/news/former-golden-state-warriors-jonas-jerebko-signs-with-new-team|website=SI.com|date=March 13, 2024 }}</ref> On April 9, he left the team after an injury.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=La Guerra del BSN|title=#BSNPR OFICIAL: El delantero Cameron Mcgriff es el nuevo refuerzo de los Santeros de Aguada en sustitución de Jonas Jerebko. Jerebko sale de la franquicia tras sufrir una lesión que lo dejará sin poder jugar de manera indefinida.|number=1777782852865638463|user=LaGuerraBSN|date=April 9, 2024|access-date=April 9, 2024|language=Spanish}}</ref>

==National team career==
[[File:SWE-CRO 20220218 Jonas Jerebko 3.jpg|thumb|Jerebko playing for Sweden in 2022]]
Jerebko debuted for the [[Sweden national basketball team|Swedish national team]] as an 18-year-old, and has since played for them at the [[EuroBasket 2013|2013 EuroBasket]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/q/jonas%20jerebko/pid//_//players.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161023012911/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/q/jonas%20jerebko/pid//_//players.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 23, 2016 |title=Jonas Jerebko – FIBA Archive |work=FIBA.com |access-date=February 14, 2016}}</ref> [[EuroBasket 2022 qualification#Group D 2|2022 EuroBasket qualifiers]], and [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Europe)|2023 World Cup qualifiers]]. Following his decision of joining [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] in the spring of 2022, Jerebko was expelled by the Swedish national team.<ref name="m.basketnews.com"/>

==Personal life==
Jerebko is the son of former [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] forward Chris Jerebko, a [[Russian American]] who played professionally in Sweden with [[Borås Basket]] for five seasons before settling in that country.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.orangehoops.org/CJerebko.htm |title=#32 Chris Jerebko |work=OrangeHoops.org |access-date=February 14, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://blog.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2009/06/jonas_jerebko_son_of_former_sy.html |title=Jonas Jerebko, son of former Syracuse University player, is on the fast track to the NBA |first=Mike |last=Waters |work=Syracuse.com |date=June 24, 2009 |access-date=February 14, 2016}}</ref> His mother also played basketball professionally.<ref name="mlive"/> 

Jerebko and his wife Johanna have two daughters and a son.<ref>{{cite web |date=January 31, 2019 |title=Embiid, 76ers spoil DeMarcus Cousins' home Warriors debut |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071441 |access-date=February 1, 2019 |work=ESPN.com |quote=Jonas Jerebko shared a photo of new daughter [...] to join big sister [...]. He planned to head back to the hospital after the game to see the baby and wife, Johanna.}}</ref>

On August 26, 2016, Jerebko purchased the [[Renegades (esports)|Renegades]] [[esports]] organization from Chris Badawi and [[MonteCristo|Christopher "MonteCristo" Mykles]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dailydot.com/esports/nba-player-buys-renegades-esports-team/|title=Boston Celtics player buys Renegades|website=dailydot.com|date=30 August 2016|access-date=20 October 2018}}</ref>
